Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: BluePixie performance handoff & acceptance cadence

Sam / BluePixie ops team —

Thanks for partnering with us on the onboarding runway. This thread is to lock the acceptance cadence and the test plan so we can move to sign-off quickly. Attached is a concise load plan (bp-load-plan-20280615.xlsx) with the scenarios we discussed. Summary below — please confirm the maintenance window and that staging keys (non-prod) will be available by Monday.

Acceptance targets (nominal):
- Model: redwood-reason-v1 (quantized)
- Steady-state throughput: 80 requests/sec (concurrent users distribution aligned with sheet)
- p95 latency: <= 150 ms end-to-end (including network to our hosted endpoint)
- p99 latency: <= 400 ms (short-term toleration up to 450 ms during cache warm-up)
- Error rate: < 0.5% (5xx / rate-limited responses excluded)

Test scenarios in the attached plan:
1) Warm-up + steady state: ramp to 80 rps over 6 minutes, hold 30 minutes
2) Burst tolerance: short spike to 200 rps for 60s to observe degradation profile
3) Cold-start probe: scale-to-zero / scale-up test during simulated cache cold state
4) Long-run stability: 3-hour run at 60 rps to validate memory growth and KV cache stability

Operational notes:
- Typical token length for BluePixie payloads: 20–48 tokens; avatar streaming disabled for tests
- We will enable request tracing and token-level cost logging in the Redwood Console; include request IDs in the test harness
- Tracing hooks and structured logs will be shared; we'll collect p50/p95/p99, tail latency, CPU/GPU utilization, and GPU batch size distribution

Attachments: bp-load-plan-20280615.xlsx (test matrix + CSV input payloads).

Next actions (please reply):
- Confirm staging credentials and maintenance window (proposed: Tue 2028-06-18 02:00–06:00 UTC)
- Confirm any firewall/VPC whitelisting for our staged load injectors
- Any constraints we should avoid during the long-run stability test (backups, deploy windows)

I'll loop engineering once we have the window.

Thanks —
Priya Natarajan
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com

Marcus — can you drive the benchmark harness and collect the console snapshots + per-request traces? Laura — please own schedule coordination and the post-run review doc.

A few clarifications to add to the plan:
- We'll use our isolated stage cluster (non-prod VPC) and test keys Sam provides; all traffic will be tagged with a run-id header for trace stitching

Attaching the Redwood benchmark runbook I recommend for this engagement (redwood-benchmark-runbook.pdf). Key test-harness details:
- Harness: vegeta + lightweight runner that hits Redwood REST endpoint; we'll also capture streaming deltas where applicable
- Auth: use staging API key + run-id header; we'll produce an envelope with request templates matching BluePixie payloads
- Ramp: 6 min ramp to target, 30 min steady-state, 60s spike at 250% of target, 3-hour soak at 60 rps for stability
- Warm-up policy: preload KV prefixes for 10 minutes prior to measurement window to avoid expected cache cold penalty
- Data capture: console snapshots, request traces, per-gpu kernel timings (where available), and raw CSV of request timings

I'll provision the runner and post the dashboard link once live.

Marcus Lin
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Team — we ran the scheduled suite earlier today. Summary (attached CSV with raw timings): bluepixie-latency-results-20280619.csv

Highlights:
- Steady-state (80 rps, 30m): p50=58ms, p95=142ms, p99=410ms
- Burst to 200 rps: sustained error rate ~0.6% during spike window (timeouts related to max inflight), recovered cleanly
- Soak at 60 rps (3h): no memory growth observed, KV hit rate stabilized at ~92% after first 20m
- Observation: p99 exceeded target (410ms vs 400ms) with short spikes coinciding with autoscale events and occasional cold-cache responses

Questions:
1) Is the p99 overshoot by 10ms an automatic fail, or do you treat this as borderline pass with a mitigation run?
2) Any quick config we can toggle in staging to reduce the autoscale-induced spikes?

I've pasted snippets of the CSV into the attached run notes. Happy to walk through live.

Sam
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sam Keating <sam.keating@bluepixie.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 16:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: BluePixie performance handoff & acceptance cadence

Sam — thanks for the thorough run and for sharing the CSV. Appreciate the fast turnaround. Notes and next steps: 

1) Acceptance stance: per our pre-agreed rule, p95 <=150ms and p99 <=400ms is an auto-sign. Since p99 is 410ms (just 2.5% over target), we recommend a conditional acceptance path:
   - Conditional sign-off granted if we complete a short targeted mitigation run that reduces autoscale flapping and warms KV cache prior to measurement window.
   - If the mitigation run shows p99 <= 400ms, we'll mark onboarding performance as accepted and proceed to the production-ready checklist.

2) Recommended mitigations (we can implement during a 30–45 minute window):
   - Increase minimum replica count in staging to avoid autoscale-triggering spikes during the measurement window (temporary change)
   - Run a 10-minute prefix warm-up script immediately prior to the measurement window (Marcus will provide command)
   - Add a short client-side retry/backoff for transient 503s during the spike test

3) Proposed follow-up: schedule a 45-minute confirmation run Wed 2028-06-21 03:00–03:45 UTC. Marcus & Ben to own runner and artifact collection; Laura to update the post-run sign-off doc.

4) Evidence package: please expect a consolidated artifact (CSV + console snapshots + trace links) posted to https://redwood.app/drive/bluepixie/onboard-plan after the run. That will be the primary acceptance evidence.

If BluePixie agrees, I'll mark the conditional sign-off and coordinate scheduling. Otherwise, we can keep iterating until we meet the target.

Thanks —
Priya
